title: Multilayer Perceptron and Backpropagation
overview: Stacking layers of neurons with nonlinearities lets a network model complex functions. Backpropagation applies the chain rule to compute the gradient of the loss for every weight efficiently.
objectives: Run a forward pass through a two-layer network
Derive gradients with the chain rule
Implement backpropagation by hand in NumPy

method.title: Forward pass
method.body: Each layer computes h = f(W x + b) and feeds its result to the next layer.

method.title: Loss
method.body: A scalar loss compares the network output with the target.

method.title: Backward pass
method.body: Gradients flow from the loss back through each layer, reusing cached forward activations.

method.title: Update
method.body: Parameters move opposite to their gradient: W -= lr * dL/dW.

pseudocode:
h = relu(X @ W1 + b1)
y_hat = h @ W2 + b2
L = mean((y_hat - y)**2)
dy = 2*(y_hat - y)/N
dW2 = h.T @ dy
dh = (dy @ W2.T) * (h > 0)
dW1 = X.T @ dh

playground.starterCode:
import numpy as np
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
X = rng.normal(size=(64, 3)); y = X.sum(axis=1, keepdims=True)
W1 = rng.normal(size=(3, 8)) * 0.5; b1 = np.zeros(8)
W2 = rng.normal(size=(8, 1)) * 0.5; b2 = np.zeros(1)
for step in range(301):
    h = np.maximum(0, X @ W1 + b1)
    pred = h @ W2 + b2
    loss = np.mean((pred - y) ** 2)
    dy = 2 * (pred - y) / len(X)
    dW2 = h.T @ dy; db2 = dy.sum(0)
    dh = (dy @ W2.T) * (h > 0)
    dW1 = X.T @ dh; db1 = dh.sum(0)
    for p, g in ((W1, dW1), (b1, db1), (W2, dW2), (b2, db2)):
        p -= 0.05 * g
    if step % 100 == 0:
        print(step, round(float(loss), 4))
